name: The Gold Agreement
summary: Nangijala did not choose a currency. It discovered the one substance nobody has ever managed to misremember.
body: Nangijala never decided on money. There was no mint, no decree, nobody with the authority to declare anything legal tender to anybody. What happened instead is that somebody eventually noticed a peculiar fact about gold, and the fact did the rest.
Gold is the only thing that everybody remembers the same.

Consider what that means in a country built the way this one is. Two people fall a thousand years and half a world apart. Ask them for a road and you will get two roads. Ask them for a house, a boat, a loaf, a king, and you will get two of each, and both will be real, and they will sit in the same field disagreeing with one another forever.
Ask them both for a gold coin and you get the same coin.

Weight, colour, the particular soft way it takes a mark from a thumbnail, the fact that it will not tarnish and will not go green and will not go anywhere at all — everybody who ever handled it came away with an identical impression, and they carried that identical impression down out of the sky. Gold is the one point in the whole of human memory where there is no argument to have.

So gold does not drift. It is the only common thing here that doesn't. Every other object in your possession is being held in shape by somebody's attention and will begin to go soft the moment that attention wanders, but a coin is a coin is a coin, and will still be exactly a coin when the house you are standing in has become a green place where a house used to be.
That is the whole reason it is money. Not scarcity — there is a great deal of it, and more falling all the time. It is money because it is the only thing you can put in a box and come back to.

There is a joke among the tellers that gold is the one honest thing in Nangijala because it is the only object nobody has ever managed to improve in the retelling. Like most jokes here it is repeated a little too often by people who are not laughing.
